newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian capital's property sector well matched.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian capital's property sector well matched.

text.p: The property market in the Indonesian capital Jakarta was well balanced despite a fast-moving economy and the volatile nature of the sector, a group of leading property consultants said on Wednesday.

Releasing the firm's quarterly outlook, Craig Williams, senior technical adviser to property consultants PT Procon Indah, said the market had more or less matched supply with demand in recent years as the capital's skyline changed rapidly.
"The fact that the market is fairly evenly balanced is a matter of good fortune more than anything else," he said.
"It has always been fairly volatile and subject to fairly rapid changes and those changes which it responds to have a lot to do with monetary policy," he told a news conference.
"Demand for property was very high in almost all sectors during 1996, but at the same time it was unable to keep pace with the higher levels of new supply," he said.
Procon Indah, in association with British-based Jones Lang Wootton, said record growth in the sector in Jakarta in 1996 was fuelled by the country's economic growth of more than seven percent a year.
"We are expecting demand to exceed new supply in 1997. That means that occupancy rates should increase by the end of this year in prime office space," Williams told reporters.
But despite this rise, he said Procon Indah predicted the average occupancy rate of office buildings in Jakarta would only increase slightly to a healthy 88 percent by the end of 1997.
Williams said occupancy levels above 95 percent would start to have an adverse effect and lead to higher rents.
The report found at the end of 1996 that total prime office stock in Jakarta had increased to 2.52 million square metres, up by 460,600 square metres from the year previously.

However, net take-up was lower than net supply in the final quarter of 1996, with the overall occupancy level decreasing to 86.3 percent from 89.3 percent three months ago and 90.2 percent in the same period in 1995.

But the report said the rate of current construction activity in the market indicated a slowing of new supply in 1997. So it projected the supply for 1997 would reach 237,825 square metres, of which 52 percent was already precomitted.
Williams said talk of oversupply in Jakarta, where cranes and construction dot the horizon, was premature.

"At the end of this year, with about 10 percent vacancy in total supply, it is equal to about one year's demand. If everybody stops building for one year, all the buildings will be full and rents will skyrocket," he said.

In the final quarter of last year, Procon Indah's selected basket of existing buildings showed average effective rents remained fairly stable at $13.50 per square metre per month, although Williams predicted this would rise slightly in 1997.
In the Jakarta retail sector, Procon Indah said occupancy was high, despite the opening of two "mega malls" late last year.

It said average occupancy at the end of 1996 remained high at 92.5 percent, two percent higher than the previous quarter. Total cumulative supply in December reached 1,004,220 square metres, an increase of 21 percent in the past 12 months.
Occupancy rates in purpose-built rental apartments and serviced apartments remained high at 83.8 percent and 76.2 percent respectively, above the overall rate for apartments of 68 percent.
